pairs.distinction: Homeless is having no reliable place to stay now; Eviction is still having a home and fearing losing it.
pairs.reason: Someone sleeping on a friend's couch and someone behind on rent know at once which one they are living with.
Having no place to stay myself and seeing more neighbors without homes are the same pain seen from the personal and societal pages, so they stay two pains linked across pages.

pairs.distinction: Eviction is the fear of losing my home; High rent is paying too much for it, which many people manage without any risk of losing it.
pairs.reason: High rent can lead to eviction, but people paying too much and people about to lose their home would each look for their own pain.

pairs.distinction: Eviction is my own home at risk; Homelessness is seeing neighbors who already have none.
pairs.reason: One is a personal fear and the other is something seen in the community, and the personal match for Homelessness is Homeless, not Eviction.

pairs.distinction: Housing is the place being cramped, broken or noisy; High rent is what it costs.
pairs.reason: Plenty of people pay too much for a decent place, and plenty live somewhere run-down that is cheap, so the choice is easy.

pairs.distinction: Heating is not being able to pay to keep warm, even in a sound home; Housing is the place itself being cramped, broken or noisy.
pairs.reason: A drafty, broken home can be cold too, but someone who can't afford the heating bill would look for that pain by name.

pairs.distinction: Heating is one specific cost going without; Rising costs is everything getting more expensive than pay.
pairs.reason: Going cold at home needs its own fixes, like heating help and insulation, and people living it would look for it rather than a general cost complaint.

pairs.distinction: Heating is going without warmth to avoid the bill; Utility bills is being behind on the bills already, which can include water.
pairs.reason: Many people keep the heat off so they never fall behind, so the alternative line 'I can't afford to keep my home warm' makes the difference clear.

pairs.distinction: Internet is not being able to get online at a decent speed or price; Transport is not being able to get to places.
pairs.reason: Both can cut people off from work and services, but nobody would confuse a slow connection with having no ride.
Not feeling safe where I live and not feeling safe from crime are the same pain seen from the personal and societal pages, so they stay two pains linked across pages.

pairs.distinction: Safety is danger in the neighborhood; Safety at home is danger from someone in my own life.
pairs.reason: The two need very different help, and the alternative name Unsafe area keeps them from both reading as Safety.
Struggling to get where I need to go and living in a place built only for cars are the same pain seen from the personal and societal pages, so they stay two pains linked across pages.
